simulatedPerson.name: veiled-light
simulatedPerson.hiddenRule: Likes frames with smoke, mist, dust or rain, or with shaped light such as beams, pools or glare (85%); otherwise 20%.

draftInterpretation: Across 85 stills from 35 films you liked 41 (48%). What follows compares the stills you liked with the ones you did not; it describes your choices in this collection, not a fixed type.

Clearly, shaped light (light that makes visible shapes: pools, beams, rim light, glare or patterned shadow): you liked 22 of 25 (88%), against 32% of the rest, across 17 films. For example: 12 Angry Men: The jurors around the table; Amélie: Amélie in the café; Double Indemnity: Keyes at his office door.

Clearly, veiled air (something in the air between camera and subject: mist, smoke, rain or dust): you liked 17 of 19 (90%), against 36% of the rest, across 13 films. For example: The Bridge on the River Kwai: The bridge over the river at dawn; Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: The War Room; Howl's Moving Castle: Howl's castle stalks across the moor under storm clouds.

Clearly, glare (a light source shines towards the lens: flare, bloom or a blazing lamp): you liked 9 of 9 (100%), against 42% of the rest, across 9 films. For example: 12 Angry Men: The jurors around the table; Amélie: Amélie in the café; Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: The War Room.

Clearly, hard light (crisp, sharp-edged shadows from a small or distant source): you liked 15 of 19 (79%), against 39% of the rest, across 11 films. For example: The Bridge on the River Kwai: Colonel Nicholson under the midday sun; Double Indemnity: Phyllis Dietrichson at the top of the stairs; Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: Major Kong settles his Stetson on in the B-52 cockpit.

Possibly, mist or haze (fog, mist or haze softens distance): you liked 7 of 7 (100%), against 44% of the rest, across 6 films. For example: The Bridge on the River Kwai: The bridge over the river at dawn; Metropolis: The city of Metropolis; Princess Mononoke: The Forest Spirit.
Some characteristics only appear to matter because they travel with the ones above: top light (accounted for by even light).
These cannot yet be told apart from the characteristics above, because they occur in nearly the same works: practical light with even light, smoke with even light and low-key with even light.
Too few examples to say anything yet about patterned shadow (2 judged), rim light (2 judged) and motion blur (2 judged).

signature.summary: A clear leaning towards shaped light, veiled air and glare. Less drawn to soft light.

terminology.label: low angle
terminology.definition: The camera looks up at the subject.

terminology.label: grand
terminology.definition: Epic in scale.

terminology.label: playful
terminology.definition: Light and whimsical.

terminology.label: clear air
terminology.definition: Nothing visible in the air.

terminology.label: mist or haze
terminology.definition: Fog, mist or haze softens distance.

terminology.label: smoke
terminology.definition: Smoke or steam drifts in the frame.

terminology.label: veiled air
terminology.definition: Something in the air between camera and subject: mist, smoke, rain or dust.

terminology.label: symmetrical composition
terminology.definition: The frame is arranged to mirror around its centre.

terminology.label: gaze at the camera
terminology.definition: The main figure looks into or very near the lens.

terminology.label: low-key
terminology.definition: Most of the frame is dark; light is selective and shadows dominate.

terminology.label: backlight
terminology.definition: Light from behind the subject, rimming or silhouetting it.

terminology.label: frontal light
terminology.definition: Light from near the camera, flattening form.

terminology.label: top light
terminology.definition: Light from above, shadowing eyes and lower forms.

terminology.label: visible beams
terminology.definition: Shafts or beams of light are visible in the air.

terminology.label: even light
terminology.definition: None of these: the light falls without distinct shapes.

terminology.label: glare
terminology.definition: A light source shines towards the lens: flare, bloom or a blazing lamp.

terminology.label: pools of light
terminology.definition: Isolated areas of light surrounded by darkness.

terminology.label: shaped light
terminology.definition: Light that makes visible shapes: pools, beams, rim light, glare or patterned shadow.

terminology.label: hard light
terminology.definition: Crisp, sharp-edged shadows from a small or distant source.

terminology.label: soft light
terminology.definition: Gradual shadow edges from a large or diffused source.

terminology.label: practical light
terminology.definition: Visible lamps, fire, candles, screens or signs within the frame.

limitations: Associations describe this person's judgments of this library only; they are not a comparison with other people.
Characteristics that always appear together in the works judged cannot be separated and are reported together.
Strength labels come from exact tests corrected for the number of characteristics tested; tentative findings may disappear with more judgments.
Findings marked subjective rest on atmosphere or tone readings, which are interpretations rather than observations.
